anti_overlap: Do not re-derive the coverage arithmetic as a finding of your own. The ledger already established that the five straw wings name 255 of 645 creatures, that 26 families and 99 unfamilied creatures fall outside them, and that a pool pre-filter would hard-gate them. Use that as input; your contribution is the intercalation rule for the residue, never the recount.

Leave the score-composition formula to the composition reviewer: how wing bias, roster kill-share heredity, and playstyle blend into one number, what precedence holds between them, the magic-number weights in calculateMatchScore, and whether getMatchedDimensions can explain the result. Your interest in composition stops at whether a cycle position is one of the inputs and whether the announcement can be checked afterward.

Do not re-litigate axis coherence as such — whether Mirrors is cut on a behavioral predicate while Funerary is cut on emotional register is the classification reviewers' ground and is already recorded. Engage the axis only where cadence, grain, or nesting actually changes the answer.
Do not review PixiJS colony rendering, the incubation ceremony's UX, Beat 2 zone or mood systems, or persistence schema design beyond the cycle position itself.

Do not report engineering-quality issues in src/sim/habitat/encryptidMatcher.ts — class structure, logging, the sourceArticle early return as a code concern. Only whether a cycle position could reach the scorer at all matters here.

Do not re-open decisions the brainstorm already ruled (pick-of-3 at extraction, incubation across the next run, options-not-power coupling, procedural rendering, two-beat shape) unless a cadence choice specifically breaks one of them.
decision_lens: Does every wing arrive on a schedule the player can come to hold, and does the scheme name every day of the year? A period the player might not see for eleven visits is a name, not a season — and a calendar with unnamed remainder days is a broken calendar, not a lenient one.
distance_rationale: Calendrics is a scheduling and reconciliation discipline, not a classification one, and that is exactly what makes it unclaimed here. Every lens already run on this design — library/faceted classification, ARPG itemization, live-service content taxonomy, perfumery family construction, heraldic marshalling — reasons about a static corpus being cut into bins and argues about where the cut lines fall. None of them has a cycle primitive at all, so none can see the possibility that the wing's real problem is cadence rather than cut. The almanac tradition's central object is a named period you live through in a known order, and its four canonical unsolved problems map one-to-one onto the four questions in this goal: how coarse to cut a continuous year (the count question), how to guarantee every named period is actually lived through (the literacy question), what to do when the named cycle refuses to tile the underlying substrate (the 390-creature residue), and how one book serves both the reader asking what a season means and the reader asking what to plant this week (the two-consumer question). It carries no library, bestiary, loot, or software vocabulary that would let the reviewer echo the design's own language back at it, and its practitioners were farmers and court astronomers rather than designers of any kind.
expected_isomorphisms: wing ↔ named solar term: a period you live through in a known order, not a label on a shelf. The per-run wing roll ↔ the substitution the design has never considered — a calendar does not roll. Grain Rain arrives; no farmer wonders whether it will come this year. The coupon-collector cost the ledger already measured (~11.4 delves in expectation to see all five wings once, f-004/f-019) is entirely an artifact of drawing from an urn, and guaranteed ordered recurrence is the mechanism that buys literacy without buying more content. Wing count ↔ the same year cut simultaneously at 4 seasons, 24 terms, and 72 pentads over one shared order, each grain read by a different user — which makes 'is five right' unanswerable without 'right for whom,' and makes nesting an alternative to picking a compromise number. The 390 roster creatures outside the straw wings ↔ intercalation: the lunar year runs ~11 days short of the solar one and the calendar does not discard the remainder, it defines a precise rule (the month containing no principal term becomes the leap month). A calendar that leaves 60% of days unnamed is not lenient, it is broken. The two consumers ↔ the almanac's two columns bound in one book and keyed to the same period names but computed by different methods: the phenological/interpretive column (what this term means, its sign, the seasonal word a poem must carry) and the prescriptive day-selection column (auspicious for planting, for building, for travel). The trade cross-referenced them for centuries and never merged them. Deterministic repetition reading as a dry streak (f-024) ↔ the parapegma's weather signs, which were stated priors with acknowledged error rather than promises, and whose authority survived being wrong because the board told the farmer to look at the sky. Wing names drifting from what runs actually produce ↔ phenological validation and calendrical drift: a term whose stated sign stops occurring is the evidence that forces reform. And the project's own canon already contains a calendar nobody has cited — §11.4's 'the weekly is a fixed-seed course — everyone reads the same room.'
focus: Whether the wing set's real unsolved problem is the cut or the cadence: whether wings should be rolled per run at all rather than advanced in a known order, at what grain and nesting they should be cut given the encounter budget a Beat 1 session actually affords, what defined rule absorbs the roster residue that no wing names, and whether one cycle can carry both an interpretive column (hatch mapping, read backward) and a prescriptive column (§11.6 loot targeting, read forward).
name: fd-almanac-seasonal-cadence
persona: Apply the perspective of a calendar and almanac maker in a pre-modern agricultural tradition — someone who cuts a continuous year into named periods that people must learn by living through them, who has watched a calendar drift out of true with the sky over centuries and be reformed at great cost, and who knows that the only reliable teacher of a period's character is its guaranteed return. This perspective treats 'how often does it come around, and in what order' as prior to 'what shall we call it.' It refuses to let a scheme of named divisions leave any part of the substrate unnamed, and reaches for an explicit intercalation rule rather than silence. It insists every period carry an observable sign so the naming can be checked against the world. It habitually keeps the column that says what a period means separate from the column that says what to do in it, cross-referenced under one set of names rather than merged. It states priors and tells the reader to look, never promises.
review_areas: Roll versus cycle — the premise nobody has examined. The brainstorm's own words are 'each delve rolls a themed wing identity,' and every literacy finding so far assumes that roll. Evaluate at least three alternatives against it: fixed rotation (wing = run index mod N), a shuffled bag with no repeat until exhaustion, and player-chosen-with-cooldown. State for each what it buys in guaranteed exposure and what it costs in surprise. Check the in-canon precedent first: §11.4 already ships a scheduled shared course ('the weekly is a fixed-seed course — everyone reads the same room'), and no prior reviewer cited it. Then price the mechanism honestly: grepping src/ for runIndex/runCount/delveCount/runsCompleted returns nothing, so no run counter exists to drive a cycle, and gearStore.ts's `afterthem.gear.v1` is the only versioned localStorage precedent for persisting the position across sessions.

Grain and nesting — whether 'is five right' is even the right question. The tradition's answer to a count argument was not a compromise number but nested grains over one shared order (4 : 24 : 72). Assess shipping a small coarse ring in Beat 1 that the deferred full Borgesrooms system subdivides later without re-cutting, against a single flat count that a later system must break. Convert the argument into a table: expected exposures per wing per sitting at 3, 5, and 7 wings, under uniform roll versus shuffled bag versus fixed rotation, using the real 180s extraction run length from the formation doc and the session lengths recorded in the teardowns doc rather than assumed ones.

Intercalation — the residue rule the design does not have. The ledger already established that the five straw wings name 255 of 645 creatures and that 99 belong to no jawnomicon family at all; treat that arithmetic as settled input and contribute the rule, not the recount. Produce a defined disposition for the remainder in calendrical terms — a named intercalary period, uniform membership across all wings, a weighted residual pool, or a coarser ring that tiles the whole corpus — and say concretely which creatures each option names, checking your own claims against families.json member lists. The test is that no creature ends up with an undefined wing value that the matcher and the later loot consumer will each invent differently.

Two columns over one cycle — the almanac shape for the dual-consumer question. Read §11.6 verbatim: 'room grammar carries targeting (funerary wings lean funerary records), so aiming the chase is knowledge, not currency.' Targeting is a forward, prescriptive act performed before a run; hatch mapping is a backward, interpretive act performed at extraction. Assess whether these are the almanac's two columns — same period names, different computations, cross-referenced, never merged — or whether they genuinely need different period sets. Say which column Beat 1 ships, what the cross-reference costs when the second arrives, and what breaks if the two are fused now.

Signs and drift — whether a wing's claim can be checked against anything. A calendrical period is validated by an observable: the term is credible because the frost, the rain, or the star-rising shows up near it. Check what the run actually puts in front of the player at extraction — RunReportSource carries elapsedTime, runKills, sidearmKills, dropsCollected, echoShards, wave.current and the formation roster, and carries no wing field — and judge whether any wing claim announced at delve start can be checked by the player against what they saw. Separately, address substrate drift: families.json is a versioned recompute (v16) and a cycle whose periods are defined by family slugs will fall out of true as the source is rebuilt; state the recalibration protocol, since real calendars drift silently for centuries when nobody defines one.

Announcement as prior, not promise — the parapegma discipline applied to the delve-start banner. The wing is announced before the run and the hatch is resolved after it. State precisely what the announcement promises, with what error band, and whether a player who gets an off-theme hatch will read it as the system lying or as weather. A schedule that claims more certainty than its mechanism has loses trust the first time it misses, and the design currently states no intended spread at all.

severity_examples.condition: Escalate to P0 when the cadence failure is structural rather than a tuning knob — no run counter exists in src/ to advance a cycle and nothing persists a position, so the roll is not a parameter someone can turn up later without new plumbing.
severity_examples.scenario: Beat 1 ships a uniform per-run wing roll with no cycle and no persisted cycle position, so at five wings the median playtest player never accumulates enough exposures for any wing to become a felt category — and the entire 'this run became this creature' legibility premise, which is the only reason wings exist in this slice, fails to land in the very beat that was meant to feel-test it.

severity_examples.condition: P1 rather than P2 because the divergence is a data-contract defect that becomes expensive once the second consumer ships, not a presentation problem.
severity_examples.scenario: The wing scheme leaves a large fraction of the roster with no defined wing value and no intercalation rule, so the implementation invents one at build time — and the hatch matcher and the later §11.6 loot-targeting consumer each invent a different one (null here, an 'unaffiliated' sentinel there, uniform membership somewhere else), producing two silently divergent taxonomies over the same names.

The count is settled by taste at a single flat grain, so the deferred full Borgesrooms system cannot subdivide the wings later without re-cutting them, and the wing vocabulary the player learned in Beat 1 has to be retrained — the exact retrofit §11.6 says the wing stand-in exists to avoid.

Wing names carry a seasonal character with no observable in-run sign, so the delve-start announcement cannot be checked against anything the run displays and reads as flavor text laid over an unrelated roll.

source_domain: Calendrical and almanac design in pre-modern agricultural traditions — the 24 solar terms (jiéqì) and 72 pentads (hòu) of the Sinitic farming calendar, lunisolar intercalation and the no-principal-term leap-month rule (無中置閏), the Greek and Roman parapegma (peg-boards of star-risings paired with weather signs), and the almanac's day-selection tables.
success_hints: Verify the mechanism gaps yourself before asserting them: grep src/ for runIndex, runCount, delveCount, runsCompleted — there is no run counter anywhere, which is what makes a cycle a plumbing question rather than a parameter. RunReportSource in src/ui/RunReport.ts carries elapsedTime, runKills, sidearmKills, dropsCollected, echoShards, wave.current and formation, and no wing field. src/sim/gearStore.ts (`afterthem.gear.v1`, guarded access, degrades on blocked storage) is the only versioned localStorage precedent in the repo — cite it when costing cycle-position persistence.

Read the canon passages verbatim rather than through the brainstorm's summary. §11.4's 'the weekly is a fixed-seed course — everyone reads the same room' is this project's own shipped precedent for scheduled shared content and no round-0 finding used it. §12.2 is the counterweight and you must engage it honestly: 'Everything else is deliberately absent from the slice: seasons, tides, events, invocation, other gods, the sport layer.' Determine whether that refusal is scoped to the shelved Watched influence slice or amounts to a standing bar against cadence, and say so plainly — do not build a recommendation that pretends the sentence is not there. §12.4's sequencing lesson (do not layer structure onto an unvalidated loop) is the live test any cycle proposal has to pass.

Do the exposure arithmetic and show the table. The formation doc records the 180s extraction run length; the teardowns doc records dwell and session shapes across the six games. Produce expected exposures per wing per sitting at 3, 5, and 7 wings under uniform roll, shuffled bag, and fixed rotation. A cadence argument without that table is an intuition; with it, the count question decides itself against a curve.

Count from /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/exports/families/v16/families.json member lists yourself before making any coverage or residue claim, and read the `rationale` fields — the ledger's 255/645 and 99-unfamilied figures are checkable and your intercalation proposal must state exactly which creatures each rule names.

Propose one concrete cycle, not an abstract argument for cadence: the named periods, their order, the grain and any nesting, the residue rule, the persisted state and what advances it, and the literal sentence shown to the player at delve start. A specific ring with the numbers attached is worth far more than a critique of rolling.

Where a cycle costs more than a roll, price it in the terms §12.4 cares about — new concepts added to a loop that has not been play-validated — and say whether the cheapest version (a shuffled bag with no new persisted state beyond one integer) captures most of the literacy benefit.
task_context:
Ideate and evaluate alternatives for the Borgesroom wing-set v0 in After Them — the themed wing identity each delve run rolls, which biases the encryptid matcher's family pools and makes run→creature hatching legible ('this run became this creature'). The current straw proposal is five tonal wings mapped to jawnomicon families: Funerary (Death-Criers/Underworld Court/Night-Comers), Tempest (Tempest-Bringers/Rain-Serpents/Rain-Holders/Maelstrom-Makers), Hearth (Hearth-Bound/Kindly Watchers/Blessing-Bearers/First Teachers), Hungers (Lurking Hunters/Hungers That Think/Monstrous Broods/Wings of Ill Omen), Mirrors (Tricksters/Shape-Thieves/Never-Caught). The four questions are: (1) Is wing-as-tonal-theme the right taxonomy axis at all? (2) Is five the right count for Beat 1, given each wing must be felt often enough to build literacy? (3) How should wing bias compose with the other hatch signals so hatches stay legible but not deterministic — and never hard-gate the 645-creature roster? (4) The wings serve TWO consumers — hatch mapping now, loot-farming literacy later (§11.6) — do the two jobs pull toward different taxonomies, and if so which taxonomy serves both?

The design under review is a brainstorm at docs/brainstorms/2026-08-09-habitat-place-brainstorm.md; the wing set is its Open Question #1 and Key Decision #9, and it is unresolved. This is a round-1 STEER-WIDE lens in a multi-round melange: five lenses have already run (faceted classification and information architecture; ARPG loot bias versus hard gates; live-service data architecture for multi-consumer taxonomies; perfumery olfactive-family construction; heraldic marshalling and cadency). Their 24 findings are settled input, not your target. They collectively established the coverage/hard-gate arithmetic, the missing composition formula, the untracked playstyle signals, the absent wing field in RunReportSource, the axis-mixing in the straw set, and the coupon-collector literacy cost. What none of them could see is that every one of them reasoned about a static corpus being cut into bins. Your mandate is the axis they have no primitive for: the wing as a period in a recurring cycle rather than a label on a shelf — cadence, order, grain and nesting, the intercalation rule for what the scheme fails to name, the observable sign that lets a naming be checked, and the almanac's two-column answer to serving two readers under one set of names.

Ground every claim in the actual sources; do not trust summaries. Primary: docs/research/2026-08-09-meta-home-loop-teardowns.md, game-design-docs/teardown-arpg-modifiers.md §§11-12 (especially 11.4, 11.6, 12.1, 12.3, 12.4), game-design-docs/after-them-delve-formation.md (R1-R8), /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/exports/families/v16/families.json (44 families with member lists and rationales), /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/data/families-prose.yaml (family blurbs), src/sim/habitat/types.ts (MediaFeatures), src/sim/habitat/encryptidMatcher.ts (scoring), src/ui/RunReport.ts (available run facts), src/sim/gearStore.ts (the persistence precedent). Grade findings P0 (would corrupt or block the whole design), P1 (a real defect that will cost significant rework), P2 (a genuine but contained problem), P3 (worth recording). Prefer a small number of grounded, arithmetic-backed findings with a concrete alternative attached over a broad sweep of plausible concerns.
